title: Mechanical waves and distant effects
target: Use travel-time reasoning while distinguishing waves from the motion of material.
criteria: Identify the medium carrying the wave.
Use speed and distance to estimate travel time.
Explain why a simple travel time does not predict damage.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: A seismic disturbance travels through rock. What is the material medium in this case?
options: The time axis on a graph.
cpa.guide: Mechanical seismic waves propagate through a material medium.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A long ocean wave passes a floating marker. Which distinction is appropriate in a simple wave model?
options: The disturbance travels across water while a water parcel moves locally.
Every parcel must travel from the source to the shore at wave speed.
The marker carries all wave energy by drifting to shore.
cpa.guide: Wave propagation differs from bulk transport of water from source to destination.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A model wave travels 360 km at a constant 180 km/h. What is travel time?
cpa.guide: t = d/v = 360/180 = 2 h with matching units.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: Sensors are 1,500 m apart along a wave path. Speed is assumed constant at 75 m/s. What arrival-time difference is expected?
cpa.guide: Δt = 1500/75 = 20 s in the stated constant-speed model.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A simple model predicts when a coastal wave arrives. What else is needed to estimate local damage?
options: Nothing; arrival time uniquely determines damage.
Wave size and energy, coastal geometry, and local exposure or vulnerability.
cpa.guide: Travel time alone does not specify wave amplitude, local amplification, or affected structures.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.

cpa.prompt: Two coastal sites have the same modeled arrival time but different shoreline shapes. Which claim is justified?
options: They need not experience the same wave height or damage.
Equal time proves equal water depth everywhere.
cpa.guide: Local geometry, depth changes, and exposure can alter the response independently of arrival time.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.
